newsitem.title: USA: Visa U.S.A. sets "zero-liability" for some lost cards.
newsitem.headline: Visa U.S.A. sets "zero-liability" for some lost cards.

text.p: Card group Visa U.S.A. said Wednesday holders of U.S. credit and check cards would be subject to zero liability if loss, theft or unauthorized use of cards was reported within two business days of discovery.
After the two-day authorization, the cardholder will be liable for a maximum of $50.
The move by Visa follows the July 30 statement from MasterCard International, a rival card group, that U.S. member banks voted to cap liability for unauthorized use of U.S. debit cards at $50.

A MasterCard spokesman said Wednesday liability for consumers is zero if loss or theft is reported in 24 hours of discovery. He said as a practical matter most card losses or theft are reported within 24 hours of discovery.

U.S. government regulations already limit cardholder liability. Regulation Z limits the liability of credit cardholders to $50 for unauthorized transactions, regardless of when loss or theft is reported.

Under Regulation E, which governs debit card transactions, consumers are liable for a maximum of $50 if the debit card is reported lost or stolen within two days of discovery, increasing to $500 if the lost or stolen debit card is reported within 60 days.
After 60 days, cardholder liability may be unlimited under certain circumstances.

Consumers Union, a non-profit group that publishes Consumer Reports, said Wednesday the Visa U.S.A. card group's newly lowered limitation on liability for lost or stolen debit cards does not go far enough.

"Unlike a credit card, a loss with an insecure debit card is instantly drained from your checking account," Gail Hillebrand, senior staff attorney for the Consumer Union's San Francisco office said in a statement. "Consumers may find themselves without a penny in their account and may face enormous bounced-check penalties as a result of theft, fraud, or error."
Visa's new policy, which commences this fall, will apply to Visa credit, Visa check cards and Interlink cards, the company said.
